evidence.location: Section 3.2, PDF p. 5, Equation 10 and cross-correlation discussion

state.target_treatment: Assignment of ground-based silver-iodide cloud seeding to Sierra Madre or Medicine Bow during a four-hour experimental unit (EU).
state.scope: The 118 quality-controlled EUs used in the WWMPP primary analysis. One EU includes the paired ranges. Target sites are HY (Sierra Madre) and GL (Medicine Bow); auxiliary gauges and possible cross-range contamination do not redefine the assigned treatment.

evidence.location: Section 2, Figure 1 explanation, and Table 1 with its caption, pp. 2640-2643
evidence.text: Within an EU, seeding is randomly assigned to one range and not the other. The authors explicitly say the Medicine Bow assignment plot would have the opposite shading from the Sierra Madre plot. The authors report 154 EUs, 27 precipitation-QC exclusions, and nine additional generator-performance exclusions, leaving 118 for the primary analysis. The monthly generator-exclusion cells in Table 1 sum to eight, while its margins and the prose report nine; the retained count here follows the authors' reported totals.

evidence.location: Section 2a and Figure 2, pp. 2642-2643
evidence.text: The design has eight generators per range and multiple precipitation gauges; gauge QC is conducted without knowledge of seeding assignments.

evidence.location: Slides 16-18, 24 and 29
evidence.text: The presentation shows the paired design, four-hour measurements, and a 118-case Medicine Bow assignment plot. Slide 24 reports ground-based ice-nucleus measurements indicating that silver iodide reached Medicine Bow in 21 Sierra Madre seeding cases. Slide 29 reports 18 modeled cases of enhanced precipitation in Medicine Bow during Sierra Madre seeding in winters 2009/10, 2011/12, and 2013/14. These are different diagnostics within the same trial reported in 2018.

criteria.permanent_range: One range is permanently assigned seeding and the other remains unseeded throughout the study.

state.target_treatment: DC-voltage calibration of the same Fluke 5700A multifunction calibrator at a common setting s, with the shared INRIM 10 V reference-standard contribution.
state.scope: Sections III-V's INRIM-Lab / Cal-Lab interlaboratory comparison. Restrict the dependence judgment to the DC-voltage traceability term in Equation 5; do not generalize it to all uncertainty components or electrical quantities.

evidence.location: Sections III.A-IV, PDF pp. 2-3; Figure 3
evidence.text: The comparison uses verification without adjustment. The Cal-Lab traceability chain shares standards calibrated at INRIM with the INRIM-Lab chain, creating partial correlation. For DC voltage, Equation 5 identifies the INRIM calibration uncertainty of the 10 V standard in both chains.

evidence.location: Section V, PDF p. 3, Equations 1-5; Conclusions, PDF p. 6
evidence.text: Cal-Lab measures before and after INRIM-Lab. Its two values at the same setting s are averaged to reduce possible calibrator drift in the comparison. The difference uncertainty includes a covariance term: u(d)^2 = u(E_L)^2 + u(E_I)^2 - 2 r u(E_L)u(E_I). Equation 5 gives r = u_B(std_DCV)^2/[u(E_I)u(E_L)]. The authors report high instrument stability.

evidence.location: Main PDF p. 6, RNA samples and RNA-seq analysis; Additional file 10
evidence.text: RNA was extracted from amygdala samples of eight female Brd1+/- mice and eight WT littermates. For each genotype, two eight-animal pools were prepared from equal RNA amounts from the same eight contributors. RNA was pooled before cDNA synthesis and library preparation. Additional file 10 labels the contributors R1-R8 and W1-W8 and shows both copies of each pool.

evidence.location: Main PDF p. 6, DEG analyses; Figure 2 caption; Additional file 10
evidence.text: The reported bulk analysis counts reads into gene-expression profiles for the prepared libraries. The study separately sequenced individual samples and three-animal pools for comparison. Those separate individual profiles are available in the study but are not observations produced by the four selected eight-animal pooled libraries.

records.record_origin: All eight pool memberships transcribed from Additional file 10. Source pool labels and contributor IDs are preserved, including W1/W3/W4 in both three-animal WT pools.

evidence.location: Methods: RNA injections into mouse zygotes; Tyr mutation analysis. Results: Characterization of CRISPR/Cas9-induced Tyr mutations
evidence.text: Tyr4a, Tyr4b, and Cas9 RNAs were introduced into zygotes. Tail-DNA analysis identified multiple mutant alleles in completely albino hybrid founder #30. The authors attribute the within-founder diversity to mosaicism, potentially arising from editing that persisted into cleavage stages. Deep sequencing reported 57 mutant alleles meeting its read-frequency threshold across 23 hybrid founders; these are not 57 injected animals.

evidence.location: Results: Germ line transmission of targeted Tyr alleles. Discussion: paragraph beginning Complete albinism and pigmentation mosaicism
evidence.text: C57BL/6N mosaics produced albino progeny in crosses with albino mates. The hybrid pigmentation mosaics were not tested this way: they already carried the FVB/NJ albino allele, which could produce albino offspring without demonstrating transmission of a newly induced allele. Somatic evidence and the C57BL/6N crosses do not establish new-allele transmission for those untested hybrids.

evidence.location: Initialization groups; Modifications incorporated in the second half
evidence.text: LENS2 has two 50-member halves: original biomass-burning forcing and an 11-year-running-mean version, SMBB, affecting 1990-2020. At each of four macro-initialization dates (1231, 1251, 1281, 1301), the first ten micro-perturbation members use original forcing and the second ten use SMBB. Ten additional even-decade initializations use original forcing; ten odd-decade initializations use SMBB.

evidence.location: Remaining modification paragraphs
evidence.text: The SMBB implementation also corrects emission-dataset issues and changes the timing of a crop-harvest carbon-flux term. The project reports no significant solution changes from the former corrections and no climate-changing impacts from the latter. Additional output fields also differ.

state.target_treatment: DC-voltage calibration of the same Fluke 5700A multifunction calibrator at a common setting s, with the shared INRIM 10 V reference-standard contribution.

evidence.location: Sections III.A-IV, PDF pp. 2-3; Figure 3
evidence.text: The comparison uses verification without adjustment. The Cal-Lab traceability chain shares standards calibrated at INRIM with the INRIM-Lab chain, creating partial correlation. For DC voltage, Equation 5 identifies the INRIM calibration uncertainty of the 10 V standard in both chains.

evidence.location: Section V, PDF p. 3, Equations 1-5; Conclusions, PDF p. 6
evidence.text: Cal-Lab measures before and after INRIM-Lab. Its two values at the same setting s are averaged to reduce possible calibrator drift in the comparison. The difference uncertainty includes a covariance term: u(d)^2 = u(E_L)^2 + u(E_I)^2 - 2 r u(E_L)u(E_I). Equation 5 gives r = u_B(std_DCV)^2/[u(E_I)u(E_L)]. The authors report high instrument stability.

state.target_treatment: Brd1 genotype-group replication in the eight-animal RNA-pooling arm.
state.scope: The four eight-animal pools: 8R pool 1/2 and 8W pool 1/2. The complete pooling figure is transcribed, but three-animal pools and individually sequenced libraries are filtered out of this claim. Genotype groups are inherited, not a claim of randomized drug administration.

evidence.location: Main PDF p. 6, RNA samples and RNA-seq analysis; Additional file 10
evidence.text: RNA was extracted from amygdala samples of eight female Brd1+/- mice and eight WT littermates. For each genotype, two eight-animal pools were prepared from equal RNA amounts from the same eight contributors. RNA was pooled before cDNA synthesis and library preparation. Additional file 10 labels the contributors R1-R8 and W1-W8 and shows both copies of each pool.

evidence.location: Main PDF p. 6, DEG analyses; Figure 2 caption; Additional file 10
evidence.text: The reported bulk analysis counts reads into gene-expression profiles for the prepared libraries. The study separately sequenced individual samples and three-animal pools for comparison. Those separate individual profiles are available in the study but are not observations produced by the four selected eight-animal pooled libraries.

records.record_origin: All eight pool memberships transcribed from Additional file 10. Source pool labels and contributor IDs are preserved, including W1/W3/W4 in both three-animal WT pools.

evidence.location: Section 2.3 and Figures 1-2, PDF pp. 4-6
evidence.text: The process refreshes recovered powder with added powder. From build 8, the authors add previously reused powder with different extents of recycling. The R index aggregates powder consumption and input history; its assumptions relate degradation to material built and exclude interactions. The paper explains why a simple reuse-cycle number is inadequate.

evidence.location: Section 2.3 final paragraphs, PDF p. 6
evidence.text: Characterized R values 0.00, 0.04, 0.15, 0.24, and 0.40 refer to virgin powder and the starts of builds 1, 3, 6, and 10, respectively, with top-up as necessary. R can increase during a build as powder is converted into solid material. The build-8 paragraph describes the addition of previously reused powder of various recycling extents.

evidence.location: Table 2, PDF p. 3
evidence.text: In the staircase protocol, the first specimen receives the starting stress. The next specimen receives a stress step down after failure or a step up after runout of the preceding specimen. Each specimen contributes one test. In the separately described step protocol, the same specimen is retested at increasing stress after runout.

evidence.location: Section 4 and Table 3, PDF p. 17; Figure 11(a), PDF p. 18

state.target_treatment: Tyr-targeted CRISPR/Cas9 zygote treatment versus replication of a defined, heritable mutant genotype.
state.scope: The hybrid (B6CBAF1/J x FVB/NJ) founder cohort: albino mouse #30 illustrates within-founder allele diversity; the germline question concerns the hybrid pigmentation mosaics. The C57BL/6N test crosses are retained as a contrasting cohort, not transferred to the hybrids.

evidence.location: Methods: RNA injections into mouse zygotes; Tyr mutation analysis. Results: Characterization of CRISPR/Cas9-induced Tyr mutations
evidence.text: Tyr4a, Tyr4b, and Cas9 RNAs were introduced into zygotes. Tail-DNA analysis identified multiple mutant alleles in completely albino hybrid founder #30. The authors attribute the within-founder diversity to mosaicism, potentially arising from editing that persisted into cleavage stages. Deep sequencing reported 57 mutant alleles meeting its read-frequency threshold across 23 hybrid founders; these are not 57 injected animals.

evidence.location: Results: Germ line transmission of targeted Tyr alleles. Discussion: paragraph beginning Complete albinism and pigmentation mosaicism
evidence.text: C57BL/6N mosaics produced albino progeny in crosses with albino mates. The hybrid pigmentation mosaics were not tested this way: they already carried the FVB/NJ albino allele, which could produce albino offspring without demonstrating transmission of a newly induced allele. Somatic evidence and the C57BL/6N crosses do not establish new-allele transmission for those untested hybrids.

records.record_origin: Source Results and Methods, as archived in NCBI BioC XML; published aggregate counts, not a new sequence reanalysis or unique-origin count. state.target_treatment: Assignment of ground-based silver-iodide cloud seeding to Sierra Madre or Medicine Bow during a four-hour experimental unit (EU).
state.scope: The 118 quality-controlled EUs used in the WWMPP primary analysis. One EU includes the paired ranges. Target sites are HY (Sierra Madre) and GL (Medicine Bow); auxiliary gauges and possible cross-range contamination do not redefine the assigned treatment.

evidence.location: Section 2, Figure 1 explanation, and Table 1 with its caption, pp. 2640-2643
evidence.text: Within an EU, seeding is randomly assigned to one range and not the other. The authors explicitly say the Medicine Bow assignment plot would have the opposite shading from the Sierra Madre plot. The authors report 154 EUs, 27 precipitation-QC exclusions, and nine additional generator-performance exclusions, leaving 118 for the primary analysis. The monthly generator-exclusion cells in Table 1 sum to eight, while its margins and the prose report nine; the retained count here follows the authors' reported totals.

evidence.location: Section 2a and Figure 2, pp. 2642-2643
evidence.text: The design has eight generators per range and multiple precipitation gauges; gauge QC is conducted without knowledge of seeding assignments.

evidence.location: Slides 16-18, 24 and 29
evidence.text: The presentation shows the paired design, four-hour measurements, and a 118-case Medicine Bow assignment plot. Slide 24 reports ground-based ice-nucleus measurements indicating that silver iodide reached Medicine Bow in 21 Sierra Madre seeding cases. Slide 29 reports 18 modeled cases of enhanced precipitation in Medicine Bow during Sierra Madre seeding in winters 2009/10, 2011/12, and 2013/14. These are different diagnostics within the same trial reported in 2018.

state.target_treatment: Assignment of ground-based silver-iodide cloud seeding to Sierra Madre or Medicine Bow during a four-hour experimental unit (EU).
state.scope: The 118 quality-controlled EUs used in the WWMPP primary analysis. One EU includes the paired ranges. Target sites are HY (Sierra Madre) and GL (Medicine Bow); auxiliary gauges and possible cross-range contamination do not redefine the assigned treatment.

evidence.location: Section 2, Figure 1 explanation, and Table 1 with its caption, pp. 2640-2643
evidence.text: Within an EU, seeding is randomly assigned to one range and not the other. The authors explicitly say the Medicine Bow assignment plot would have the opposite shading from the Sierra Madre plot. The authors report 154 EUs, 27 precipitation-QC exclusions, and nine additional generator-performance exclusions, leaving 118 for the primary analysis. The monthly generator-exclusion cells in Table 1 sum to eight, while its margins and the prose report nine; the retained count here follows the authors' reported totals.

evidence.location: Section 2a and Figure 2, pp. 2642-2643
evidence.text: The design has eight generators per range and multiple precipitation gauges; gauge QC is conducted without knowledge of seeding assignments.

evidence.location: Slides 16-18, 24 and 29
evidence.text: The presentation shows the paired design, four-hour measurements, and a 118-case Medicine Bow assignment plot. Slide 24 reports ground-based ice-nucleus measurements indicating that silver iodide reached Medicine Bow in 21 Sierra Madre seeding cases. Slide 29 reports 18 modeled cases of enhanced precipitation in Medicine Bow during Sierra Madre seeding in winters 2009/10, 2011/12, and 2013/14. These are different diagnostics within the same trial reported in 2018.

state.target_treatment: Tyr-targeted CRISPR/Cas9 zygote treatment versus replication of a defined, heritable mutant genotype.
state.scope: The hybrid (B6CBAF1/J x FVB/NJ) founder cohort: albino mouse #30 illustrates within-founder allele diversity; the germline question concerns the hybrid pigmentation mosaics. The C57BL/6N test crosses are retained as a contrasting cohort, not transferred to the hybrids.

evidence.location: Methods: RNA injections into mouse zygotes; Tyr mutation analysis. Results: Characterization of CRISPR/Cas9-induced Tyr mutations
evidence.text: Tyr4a, Tyr4b, and Cas9 RNAs were introduced into zygotes. Tail-DNA analysis identified multiple mutant alleles in completely albino hybrid founder #30. The authors attribute the within-founder diversity to mosaicism, potentially arising from editing that persisted into cleavage stages. Deep sequencing reported 57 mutant alleles meeting its read-frequency threshold across 23 hybrid founders; these are not 57 injected animals.

evidence.location: Results: Germ line transmission of targeted Tyr alleles. Discussion: paragraph beginning Complete albinism and pigmentation mosaicism
evidence.text: C57BL/6N mosaics produced albino progeny in crosses with albino mates. The hybrid pigmentation mosaics were not tested this way: they already carried the FVB/NJ albino allele, which could produce albino offspring without demonstrating transmission of a newly induced allele. Somatic evidence and the C57BL/6N crosses do not establish new-allele transmission for those untested hybrids.

records.record_origin: Source Results and Methods, as archived in NCBI BioC XML; published aggregate counts, not a new sequence reanalysis or unique-origin count. The value 5 for founder #30 is the author-manuscript prose report; publisher Figure 3C lists six allele entries. The exact total remains unresolved.

evidence.location: Section V, PDF p. 3, Equations 1-5; Conclusions, PDF p. 6
evidence.text: Cal-Lab measures before and after INRIM-Lab. Its two values at the same setting s are averaged to reduce possible calibrator drift in the comparison. state.target_treatment: The original gestational dioxin (TCDD) injection regimen, distinguished from descendant lineage membership.
state.scope: The Dioxin row in Supplemental Tables S1B and S1C, generations F1-F3, and the original F0 gestational exposure. Other chemicals, toxicity outcomes, effect sizes, and mechanisms of inheritance are outside this claim.

evidence.location: Main PDF p. 2, Results; p. 9, treatment and breeding methods
evidence.text: Only pregnant F0 rats received the experimental injections, during embryonic days 8-14. F1 animals were bred within exposure lineage to produce F2, and F2 produced F3; sibling and cousin crosses were avoided. The paper distinguishes the injected F0 mother, the directly exposed F1 embryo, and the germ cells inside that embryo that will generate F2. F3 lies beyond this original direct-exposure window under the paper's generational definition.

evidence.location: Supplemental Table S1B, PDF p. 1; Table S1C, PDF p. 2; Dioxin row
evidence.text: The Dioxin lineage has 4, 14, and 14 weaned litters in F1, F2, and F3. Female/male pup counts are 15/20, 68/78, and 84/78, respectively. These are descendant census records, not a register of newly injected animals or individual pedigrees.

state.scope: Table 1 experiment 11a versus Table 2 experiment 11, with the source's mutation-and-clonal-growth interpretation. Other experiment columns and mutation-rate estimation are excluded.

evidence.location: Printed pp. 502-504 (PDF pp. 12-14), plating methods, Table 1 and Table 2
evidence.text: Table 1 uses parallel platings of samples from the same grown culture to check sampling and plating variability. Table 2 uses cultures grown separately in parallel before testing. In experiment 11a the ten resistant-colony counts are 46, 56, 52, 48, 65, 44, 49, 51, 56, 47. In experiment 11 they are 30, 10, 40, 45, 183, 12, 173, 23, 57, 51.

evidence.location: Printed pp. 493, 496 and 507-508 (PDF pp. 3, 6 and 17-18)
evidence.text: Under the mutation interpretation, resistance can arise before virus exposure and be inherited by descendants. Early mutations can therefore contribute many resistant cells. The paper distinguishes mutation events from their descendants and interprets the fluctuations using clonal relatedness. Neither selected table assigns colonies to individual mutation origins.

state.target_treatment: Original CMIP6 biomass-burning forcing versus the revised SMBB implementation in CESM2-LENS2.
state.scope: All 100 documented LENS2 members, with the forcing change during 1990-2020. Member groups and initialization dates follow the official page; no independent climate-state count is inferred from output fields.

evidence.location: Initialization groups; Modifications incorporated in the second half
evidence.text: LENS2 has two 50-member halves: original biomass-burning forcing and an 11-year-running-mean version, SMBB, affecting 1990-2020. At each of four macro-initialization dates (1231, 1251, 1281, 1301), the first ten micro-perturbation members use original forcing and the second ten use SMBB. Ten additional even-decade initializations use original forcing; ten odd-decade initializations use SMBB.

evidence.location: Remaining modification paragraphs
evidence.text: The SMBB implementation also corrects emission-dataset issues and changes the timing of a crop-harvest carbon-flux term. The project reports no significant solution changes from the former corrections and no climate-changing impacts from the latter. Additional output fields also differ.

evidence.location: Main PDF p. 6, RNA samples and RNA-seq analysis; Additional file 10
evidence.text: RNA was extracted from amygdala samples of eight female Brd1+/- mice and eight WT littermates. For each genotype, two eight-animal pools were prepared from equal RNA amounts from the same eight contributors. RNA was pooled before cDNA synthesis and library preparation. Additional file 10 labels the contributors R1-R8 and W1-W8 and shows both copies of each pool.

evidence.location: Main PDF p. 6, DEG analyses; Figure 2 caption; Additional file 10
evidence.text: The reported bulk analysis counts reads into gene-expression profiles for the prepared libraries. The study separately sequenced individual samples and three-animal pools for comparison. Those separate individual profiles are available in the study but are not observations produced by the four selected eight-animal pooled libraries.

records.record_origin: All eight pool memberships transcribed from Additional file 10. Source pool labels and contributor IDs are preserved, including W1/W3/W4 in both three-animal WT pools.

evidence.location: Section 2.3 and Figures 1-2, PDF pp. 4-6
evidence.text: The process refreshes recovered powder with added powder. From build 8, the authors add previously reused powder with different extents of recycling. evidence.location: Section 2.3 final paragraphs, PDF p. 6

R can increase during a build as powder is converted into solid material. The build-8 paragraph describes the addition of previously reused powder of various recycling extents.

state.target_treatment: Independent pre-selection culture growth histories and the interpretation of resistance after phage selection.
state.scope: Table 1 experiment 11a versus Table 2 experiment 11, with the source's mutation-and-clonal-growth interpretation. Other experiment columns and mutation-rate estimation are excluded.

evidence.location: Printed pp. 502-504 (PDF pp. 12-14), plating methods, Table 1 and Table 2
evidence.text: Table 1 uses parallel platings of samples from the same grown culture to check sampling and plating variability. Table 2 uses cultures grown separately in parallel before testing. In experiment 11a the ten resistant-colony counts are 46, 56, 52, 48, 65, 44, 49, 51, 56, 47. In experiment 11 they are 30, 10, 40, 45, 183, 12, 173, 23, 57, 51.

evidence.location: Printed pp. 493, 496 and 507-508 (PDF pp. 3, 6 and 17-18)
evidence.text: Under the mutation interpretation, resistance can arise before virus exposure and be inherited by descendants. Early mutations can therefore contribute many resistant cells. The paper distinguishes mutation events from their descendants and interprets the fluctuations using clonal relatedness. Neither selected table assigns colonies to individual mutation origins.

records.record_origin: Original row order checked visually in both scanned tables. Experiment 11a and 11 are distinct source labels; row indices identify samples or cultures according to the table.

state.target_treatment: Assignment of ground-based silver-iodide cloud seeding to Sierra Madre or Medicine Bow during a four-hour experimental unit (EU).
state.scope: The 118 quality-controlled EUs used in the WWMPP primary analysis. One EU includes the paired ranges. Target sites are HY (Sierra Madre) and GL (Medicine Bow); auxiliary gauges and possible cross-range contamination do not redefine the assigned treatment.

evidence.location: Section 2, Figure 1 explanation, and Table 1 with its caption, pp. 2640-2643
evidence.text: Within an EU, seeding is randomly assigned to one range and not the other. The authors explicitly say the Medicine Bow assignment plot would have the opposite shading from the Sierra Madre plot. The authors report 154 EUs, 27 precipitation-QC exclusions, and nine additional generator-performance exclusions, leaving 118 for the primary analysis. The monthly generator-exclusion cells in Table 1 sum to eight, while its margins and the prose report nine; the retained count here follows the authors' reported totals.

evidence.location: Section 2a and Figure 2, pp. 2642-2643
evidence.text: The design has eight generators per range and multiple precipitation gauges; gauge QC is conducted without knowledge of seeding assignments.

evidence.location: Slides 16-18, 24 and 29
evidence.text: The presentation shows the paired design, four-hour measurements, and a 118-case Medicine Bow assignment plot. Slide 24 reports ground-based ice-nucleus measurements indicating that silver iodide reached Medicine Bow in 21 Sierra Madre seeding cases. Slide 29 reports 18 modeled cases of enhanced precipitation in Medicine Bow during Sierra Madre seeding in winters 2009/10, 2011/12, and 2013/14. These are different diagnostics within the same trial reported in 2018.

evidence.text: RNA was extracted from amygdala samples of eight female Brd1+/- mice and eight WT littermates. state.target_treatment: Original CMIP6 biomass-burning forcing versus the revised SMBB implementation in CESM2-LENS2.
state.scope: All 100 documented LENS2 members, with the forcing change during 1990-2020. Member groups and initialization dates follow the official page; no independent climate-state count is inferred from output fields.

evidence.location: Initialization groups; Modifications incorporated in the second half
evidence.text: LENS2 has two 50-member halves: original biomass-burning forcing and an 11-year-running-mean version, SMBB, affecting 1990-2020. At each of four macro-initialization dates (1231, 1251, 1281, 1301), the first ten micro-perturbation members use original forcing and the second ten use SMBB. Ten additional even-decade initializations use original forcing; ten odd-decade initializations use SMBB.

evidence.location: Remaining modification paragraphs
evidence.text: The SMBB implementation also corrects emission-dataset issues and changes the timing of a crop-harvest carbon-flux term. The project reports no significant solution changes from the former corrections and no climate-changing impacts from the latter. Additional output fields also differ.

state.target_treatment: DC-voltage calibration of the same Fluke 5700A multifunction calibrator at a common setting s, with the shared INRIM 10 V reference-standard contribution.
state.scope: Sections III-V's INRIM-Lab / Cal-Lab interlaboratory comparison. Restrict the dependence judgment to the DC-voltage traceability term in Equation 5; do not generalize it to all uncertainty components or electrical quantities.

evidence.location: Sections III.A-IV, PDF pp. 2-3; Figure 3
evidence.text: The comparison uses verification without adjustment. The Cal-Lab traceability chain shares standards calibrated at INRIM with the INRIM-Lab chain, creating partial correlation. For DC voltage, Equation 5 identifies the INRIM calibration uncertainty of the 10 V standard in both chains.

evidence.location: Section V, PDF p. 3, Equations 1-5; Conclusions, PDF p. 6
evidence.text: Cal-Lab measures before and after INRIM-Lab. Its two values at the same setting s are averaged to reduce possible calibrator drift in the comparison. The difference uncertainty includes a covariance term: u(d)^2 = u(E_L)^2 + u(E_I)^2 - 2 r u(E_L)u(E_I). Equation 5 gives r = u_B(std_DCV)^2/[u(E_I)u(E_L)]. The authors report high instrument stability.

evidence.location: Table 2, PDF p. 3
evidence.text: In the staircase protocol, the first specimen receives the starting stress. evidence.location: Section 4 and Table 3, PDF p. 17; Figure 11(a), PDF p. 18

state.target_treatment: Recycling history of Ti-6Al-4V feedstock used in the LPBF top-up process.
state.scope: Section 2.3's build-8-and-later top-up regime through build 10. The question concerns feedstock provenance, not the number of tensile specimens or scan tracks.

evidence.location: Section 2.3 and Figures 1-2, PDF pp. 4-6
evidence.text: The process refreshes recovered powder with added powder. From build 8, the authors add previously reused powder with different extents of recycling. The R index aggregates powder consumption and input history; its assumptions relate degradation to material built and exclude interactions. The paper explains why a simple reuse-cycle number is inadequate.

evidence.location: Section 2.3 final paragraphs, PDF p. 6
evidence.text: Characterized R values 0.00, 0.04, 0.15, 0.24, and 0.40 refer to virgin powder and the starts of builds 1, 3, 6, and 10, respectively, with top-up as necessary. R can increase during a build as powder is converted into solid material. The build-8 paragraph describes the addition of previously reused powder of various recycling extents.

evidence.location: Main PDF p. 2, Results; p. 9, treatment and breeding methods
evidence.text: Only pregnant F0 rats received the experimental injections, during embryonic days 8-14. F1 animals were bred within exposure lineage to produce F2, and F2 produced F3; sibling and cousin crosses were avoided. The paper distinguishes the injected F0 mother, the directly exposed F1 embryo, and the germ cells inside that embryo that will generate F2. F3 lies beyond this original direct-exposure window under the paper's generational definition.

evidence.location: Supplemental Table S1B, PDF p. 1; Table S1C, PDF p. 2; Dioxin row
evidence.text: The Dioxin lineage has 4, 14, and 14 weaned litters in F1, F2, and F3. Female/male pup counts are 15/20, 68/78, and 84/78, respectively. These are descendant census records, not a register of newly injected animals or individual pedigrees.

evidence.location: Methods: RNA injections into mouse zygotes; Tyr mutation analysis. Results: Characterization of CRISPR/Cas9-induced Tyr mutations
evidence.text: Tyr4a, Tyr4b, and Cas9 RNAs were introduced into zygotes. Tail-DNA analysis identified multiple mutant alleles in completely albino hybrid founder #30. The authors attribute the within-founder diversity to mosaicism, potentially arising from editing that persisted into cleavage stages. Deep sequencing reported 57 mutant alleles meeting its read-frequency threshold across 23 hybrid founders; these are not 57 injected animals.

evidence.location: Results: Germ line transmission of targeted Tyr alleles. Discussion: paragraph beginning Complete albinism and pigmentation mosaicism
evidence.text: C57BL/6N mosaics produced albino progeny in crosses with albino mates. The hybrid pigmentation mosaics were not tested this way: they already carried the FVB/NJ albino allele, which could produce albino offspring without demonstrating transmission of a newly induced allele. Somatic evidence and the C57BL/6N crosses do not establish new-allele transmission for those untested hybrids.

state.scope: Sections III-V's INRIM-Lab / Cal-Lab interlaboratory comparison. Restrict the dependence judgment to the DC-voltage traceability term in Equation 5; do not generalize it to all uncertainty components or electrical quantities.

evidence.location: Sections III.A-IV, PDF pp. 2-3; Figure 3
evidence.text: The comparison uses verification without adjustment. The Cal-Lab traceability chain shares standards calibrated at INRIM with the INRIM-Lab chain, creating partial correlation. For DC voltage, Equation 5 identifies the INRIM calibration uncertainty of the 10 V standard in both chains.

evidence.location: Section V, PDF p. 3, Equations 1-5; Conclusions, PDF p. 6
evidence.text: Cal-Lab measures before and after INRIM-Lab. Its two values at the same setting s are averaged to reduce possible calibrator drift in the comparison. The difference uncertainty includes a covariance term: u(d)^2 = u(E_L)^2 + u(E_I)^2 - 2 r u(E_L)u(E_I). Equation 5 gives r = u_B(std_DCV)^2/[u(E_I)u(E_L)]. The authors report high instrument stability.

evidence.location: Printed pp. 502-504 (PDF pp. 12-14), plating methods, Table 1 and Table 2
evidence.text: Table 1 uses parallel platings of samples from the same grown culture to check sampling and plating variability. Table 2 uses cultures grown separately in parallel before testing. evidence.location: Printed pp. 493, 496 and 507-508 (PDF pp. 3, 6 and 17-18)

records.record_origin: Original row order checked visually in both scanned tables. Experiment 11a and 11 are distinct source labels; row indices identify samples or cultures according to the table.

state.target_treatment: Applied fatigue stress in the regular staircase test of 304L stainless-steel foil specimens.
state.scope: Table 2's staircase/up-down protocol as implemented in Section 4 and Figure 11(a). Figure 11(b-d) are other protocols, not additional observations of the selected allocation rule.

evidence.location: Table 2, PDF p. 3
evidence.text: In the staircase protocol, the first specimen receives the starting stress. The next specimen receives a stress step down after failure or a step up after runout of the preceding specimen. Each specimen contributes one test. In the separately described step protocol, the same specimen is retested at increasing stress after runout.

evidence.location: Section 4 and Table 3, PDF p. 17; Figure 11(a), PDF p. 18
evidence.text: The experimental material is 304L foil. Specimens were extracted randomly across the foil and assigned to protocols in randomized order to reduce time effects. Table 3 states a 325 MPa start and 30 MPa steps. Figure 11(a) plots the regular staircase sequence; the caption also states 30 MPa increments. The rendered table and figure accompany this evidence.

evidence.location: Section 2.3 and Figures 1-2, PDF pp. 4-6
evidence.text: The process refreshes recovered powder with added powder. From build 8, the authors add previously reused powder with different extents of recycling. The R index aggregates powder consumption and input history; its assumptions relate degradation to material built and exclude interactions. The paper explains why a simple reuse-cycle number is inadequate.

evidence.location: Section 2.3 final paragraphs, PDF p. 6
evidence.text: Characterized R values 0.00, 0.04, 0.15, 0.24, and 0.40 refer to virgin powder and the starts of builds 1, 3, 6, and 10, respectively, with top-up as necessary. R can increase during a build as powder is converted into solid material. The build-8 paragraph describes the addition of previously reused powder of various recycling extents.

state.target_treatment: Assignment of ground-based silver-iodide cloud seeding to Sierra Madre or Medicine Bow during a four-hour experimental unit (EU).
state.scope: The 118 quality-controlled EUs used in the WWMPP primary analysis. One EU includes the paired ranges. Target sites are HY (Sierra Madre) and GL (Medicine Bow); auxiliary gauges and possible cross-range contamination do not redefine the assigned treatment.

evidence.location: Section 2, Figure 1 explanation, and Table 1 with its caption, pp. 2640-2643
evidence.text: Within an EU, seeding is randomly assigned to one range and not the other. The authors explicitly say the Medicine Bow assignment plot would have the opposite shading from the Sierra Madre plot. The authors report 154 EUs, 27 precipitation-QC exclusions, and nine additional generator-performance exclusions, leaving 118 for the primary analysis. The monthly generator-exclusion cells in Table 1 sum to eight, while its margins and the prose report nine; the retained count here follows the authors' reported totals.

evidence.location: Section 2a and Figure 2, pp. 2642-2643
evidence.text: The design has eight generators per range and multiple precipitation gauges; gauge QC is conducted without knowledge of seeding assignments.

evidence.location: Slides 16-18, 24 and 29
evidence.text: The presentation shows the paired design, four-hour measurements, and a 118-case Medicine Bow assignment plot. Slide 24 reports ground-based ice-nucleus measurements indicating that silver iodide reached Medicine Bow in 21 Sierra Madre seeding cases. Slide 29 reports 18 modeled cases of enhanced precipitation in Medicine Bow during Sierra Madre seeding in winters 2009/10, 2011/12, and 2013/14. These are different diagnostics within the same trial reported in 2018.

criteria.complementary_assignment: One joint allocation selects the seeded range, and the other range receives the complementary unseeded assignment.
criteria.both_seeded: Both ranges are assigned seeding together as one treated pair.
criteria.permanent_range: One range is permanently assigned seeding and the other remains unseeded throughout the study.

state.target_treatment: Brd1 genotype-group replication in the eight-animal RNA-pooling arm.
state.scope: The four eight-animal pools: 8R pool 1/2 and 8W pool 1/2. The complete pooling figure is transcribed, but three-animal pools and individually sequenced libraries are filtered out of this claim. Genotype groups are inherited, not a claim of randomized drug administration.

evidence.location: Main PDF p. 6, RNA samples and RNA-seq analysis; Additional file 10
evidence.text: RNA was extracted from amygdala samples of eight female Brd1+/- mice and eight WT littermates. For each genotype, two eight-animal pools were prepared from equal RNA amounts from the same eight contributors. RNA was pooled before cDNA synthesis and library preparation. Additional file 10 labels the contributors R1-R8 and W1-W8 and shows both copies of each pool.

evidence.location: Main PDF p. 6, DEG analyses; Figure 2 caption; Additional file 10
evidence.text: The reported bulk analysis counts reads into gene-expression profiles for the prepared libraries. The study separately sequenced individual samples and three-animal pools for comparison. Those separate individual profiles are available in the study but are not observations produced by the four selected eight-animal pooled libraries.

records.record_origin: All eight pool memberships transcribed from Additional file 10. Source pool labels and contributor IDs are preserved, including W1/W3/W4 in both three-animal WT pools.

state.target_treatment: Paired-fixed initialization for the N1000 cosmological N-body simulation set.
state.scope: Only the 100 paired-fixed realizations in Table 1's N1000 row; exclude its 100 standard realizations and all other simulation sets. One paired-fixed realization contains two phase-related executions.

evidence.location: Section 2, PDF pp. 2-3; Table 1, PDF p. 4
evidence.text: The two fixed fields of a pair use the same fixed Fourier amplitudes, with phases shifted by pi between them. Table 1 lists 100 N1000 paired-fixed realizations and states that each corresponds to two simulations. The simulations are separate executions, not two output snapshots of one execution.

evidence.location: Section 3.2, PDF p. 5, Equation 10 and cross-correlation discussion
evidence.text: The authors first average the two simulations' values for a paired-fixed realization, then calculate statistics across realizations. They explicitly analyze the cross-correlation within pairs. Phase flipping does not imply that every evolved observable has perfect negative correlation.

state.target_treatment: Original CMIP6 biomass-burning forcing versus the revised SMBB implementation in CESM2-LENS2.
state.scope: All 100 documented LENS2 members, with the forcing change during 1990-2020. Member groups and initialization dates follow the official page; no independent climate-state count is inferred from output fields.

evidence.location: Initialization groups; Modifications incorporated in the second half
evidence.text: LENS2 has two 50-member halves: original biomass-burning forcing and an 11-year-running-mean version, SMBB, affecting 1990-2020. At each of four macro-initialization dates (1231, 1251, 1281, 1301), the first ten micro-perturbation members use original forcing and the second ten use SMBB. Ten additional even-decade initializations use original forcing; ten odd-decade initializations use SMBB.

evidence.location: Remaining modification paragraphs
evidence.text: The SMBB implementation also corrects emission-dataset issues and changes the timing of a crop-harvest carbon-flux term. The project reports no significant solution changes from the former corrections and no climate-changing impacts from the latter. Additional output fields also differ.

state.target_treatment: Original CMIP6 biomass-burning forcing versus the revised SMBB implementation in CESM2-LENS2.
state.scope: All 100 documented LENS2 members, with the forcing change during 1990-2020. Member groups and initialization dates follow the official page; no independent climate-state count is inferred from output fields.

evidence.location: Initialization groups; Modifications incorporated in the second half
evidence.text: LENS2 has two 50-member halves: original biomass-burning forcing and an 11-year-running-mean version, SMBB, affecting 1990-2020. At each of four macro-initialization dates (1231, 1251, 1281, 1301), the first ten micro-perturbation members use original forcing and the second ten use SMBB. Ten additional even-decade initializations use original forcing; ten odd-decade initializations use SMBB.

evidence.location: Remaining modification paragraphs
evidence.text: The SMBB implementation also corrects emission-dataset issues and changes the timing of a crop-harvest carbon-flux term. The project reports no significant solution changes from the former corrections and no climate-changing impacts from the latter. Additional output fields also differ.
